author: cpubot
body:
#### Problem

##### Load shedding

In gossip, channels in `run_listen` and `run_socket_consume` are continuously drained on the receiving side while packets are being received. 

https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/2cd02bb18ec8874c4d0ec18f5390f93298ebdbb4/gossip/src/cluster_info.rs#L2104-L2119

In principle, nothing prevents the outer `for` loop from running for an extended period if packets keep arriving. 
> _However, practically speaking, implicit system conditions (e.g., thread scheduling, crossbeam internal synchronization) will eventually cause it to terminate._

This can introduce non-trivial lag time between packets being received and processed under high load. I.e., we will just keep dropping packets under sufficient load without making progress.

##### Variable and potentially high number of packet batches dropped per loop

Because channel draining may pull up to `MAX_GOSSIP_TRAFFIC` packet batches, we don't have predictable / governed dropping pressure. 

> _For example, taking the avg packet batch size, 28 * MAX_GOSSIP_TRAFFIC = 3711 packet batches._

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/511e5cf5-6226-49e8-9def-cca74c18903c)

Note the white gaps correlated to spikes in `solGossipConsum`. These represent stalls in gossip consumer threads due to memory reclamation.

#### Summary of Changes

##### Load shedding

Load shedding now occurs on the sending side. A trait, `ChannelSend`, is introduced to allow abstracting over `send`/`try_send` implementations. 

- An implementation of `ChannelSend`, `EvictingSender`, which drops older packets in favor of newer packets, is added to gossip.
- A default implementation of `ChannelSend` for `crossbeam_channel::Sender` is added so that existing users of `streamer::receiver` maintain existing behavior and don't need to depend on new concrete type, while allowing gossip to implement its own drop behavior.
- Channel sizes are reduced to `4096` since ingress is now governed by channel size.
    - This is `262,144` packets with saturated packet batches (64 packets).
    - `114,688` packets with observed average packet batch size (28 packets), putting this within reasonable range of previous hard limit of `MAX_GOSSIP_TRAFFIC` (`103,896`).

##### Variable and potentially high number of packet batches dropped per loop

Because load shedding occurs on the sending side, channel receivers can pull smaller, fixed sized sets of packet batches without negatively impacting throughput. Load shedding occurs concurrently with processing, rather than processing being blocked until the channel is drained.
> _Contrast this to master where throughput and batch processing size are governed by the same constant, `MAX_GOSSIP_TRAFFIC`._

Channel receivers in `run_socket_consume` and `run_listen` now pull a fixed `1024` packet batches per iteration, providing consistent / predictable dropping pressure and eliminating current worst case behavior.

author: streamer45
body:
#### Summary

I've finally decided to try to eliminate the various race conditions that still affect signaling because the server side does not implement the [perfect negotiation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebRTC_API/Perfect_negotiation) pattern.

My [previous statement](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost-plugin-calls/pull/870#discussion_r1784648708) on this topic was not entirely accurate. Even the browser side could still get into an invalid SDP state. It was just more rare, but it was still fairly reproducible when dealing with more than a single audio track.

Anyhow, to get rid of all of this, we implement a synchronization mechanism (lock) through our data channel.

#### Related PR

https://github.com/mattermost/calls-common/pull/45

#### Ticket Link

https://mattermost.atlassian.net/browse/MM-62296

This adds our native read for S3 Tables along with the remaining catalogs APIs. Because we have implemented `get_table` and the catalog interface, we can attach to sessions and execute SQL against S3 Tables. This pull request introduces significant updates to the ChatDesk application, including enhancements to the documentation, API improvements, and updates to the chat model handling. The most important changes are grouped into documentation updates and code improvements.

### Documentation Updates:
* [`.github/copilot-instructions.md`](diffhunk://#diff-227c2c26cb2ee0ce0f46a320fc48fbcbdf21801a57f59161b1d0861e8aad55f5R1-R30): Added detailed instructions in Chinese for the role of a senior full-stack engineer and the development of the ChatDesk application, including front-end and back-end requirements, and other development guidelines.
* [`README.md`](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L1-R149): Updated the README to reflect the new ChatDesk branding, added detailed descriptions of the main features, technology stack, model providers, deployment instructions, local development setup, database operations, contribution guidelines, and license information.

### Code Improvements:
* [`app/(chat)/actions.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-dff065efa453f768e9b513f8f04b0f8ae854fbea4eef08279de48e41597dc760L3-R65): Updated the `saveChatModelAsCookie` function to support saving custom model information, and modified the `generateTitleFromUserMessage` function to use the selected model ID.
* [`app/(chat)/api/chat/route.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-dee1550b5ed5afa23c207445438b6542ca172911418ae471e2e285f01ada6469L5-L9): Refactored the chat API routes to use the selected language model and removed unused imports and tools. Updated the POST method to pass the selected model ID to the title generation function. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-dee1550b5ed5afa23c207445438b6542ca172911418ae471e2e285f01ada6469L5-L9) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-dee1550b5ed5afa23c207445438b6542ca172911418ae471e2e285f01ada6469L24-R22) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-dee1550b5ed5afa23c207445438b6542ca172911418ae471e2e285f01ada6469L36-R35) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-dee1550b5ed5afa23c207445438b6542ca172911418ae471e2e285f01ada6469L54-R56) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-dee1550b5ed5afa23c207445438b6542ca172911418ae471e2e285f01ada6469L63-R93) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-dee1550b5ed5afa23c207445438b6542ca172911418ae471e2e285f01ada6469L157-R162)
* [`app/(chat)/api/models/route.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-cf3e8e6ed82250c9647192006e8cdae9307adfaad56a1f746e2361b2dc6306e3R1-R43): Added a new route to fetch models by provider ID for the authenticated user.
* `app/(chat)/chat/[id]/page.tsx` and `app/(chat)/page.tsx`: Updated the chat pages to handle custom model information, including fetching user-configured models and setting the default model if none is selected. ([app/(chat)/chat/[id]/page.tsxL2-R8](diffhunk://#diff-febd1062898f083f38daa92c2b8408785a87424badf561fb7ee14e6ed8e4e063L2-R8), [app/(chat)/chat/[id]/page.tsxL21-L26](diffhunk://#diff-febd1062898f083f38daa92c2b8408785a87424badf561fb7ee14e6ed8e4e063L21-L26), [app/(chat)/chat/[id]/page.tsxR35-R87](diffhunk://#diff-febd1062898f083f38daa92c2b8408785a87424badf561fb7ee14e6ed8e4e063R35-R87), [app/(chat)/chat/[id]/page.tsxR102-R103](diffhunk://#diff-febd1062898f083f38daa92c2b8408785a87424badf561fb7ee14e6ed8e4e063R102-R103), [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f4633d621567bbfd891aa5c88d7dc9c234ace0f5e61861c74a5c59972ab11035L2-R71) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f4633d621567bbfd891aa5c88d7dc9c234ace0f5e61861c74a5c59972ab11035R81-R82)

body: ## Description In a Card component, when the `toggles` boolean property is specified: 1. the checkbox that displays on hover must have an accessibility name. 2. the checkbox should be keyboard focusable To fix these issues, remove `tabIndex="-1"` and include the header text as a hidden accessible name for the sp-checkbox at: https://github.com/adobe/spectrum-web-components/blob/e7d153e653da03fbceb0c5a605bc6e2f6d21ca3a/packages/card/src/Card.ts#L318-L323 ```js ${this.heading} ``` The `.sr-only` style, and a `--mod-checkbox-text-to-control` override to account for the fact that the text label is visually hidden, should be added to the [card.css](https://github.com/adobe/spectrum-web-components/blob/main/packages/card/src/card.css) file: ```css .checkbox-toggle .checkbox { --mod-checkbox-text-to-control: 0; } .sr-only { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding: 0; margin: -1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0); white-space: nowrap; border: 0; } ``` At present, this is the only way to appropriately label a `sp-checkbox`. 3. Similarly, in the storybook examples using the Card with an action button, the action button should be keyboard focusable. Again, we need to remove `tabIndex="-1"` from the `sp-action-menu` in Card rendering for the Storybook example: https://github.com/adobe/spectrum-web-components/blob/e7d153e653da03fbceb0c5a605bc6e2f6d21ca3a/tools/grid/stories/grid.stories.ts#L77-L83 ```js ``` ## Related issue(s) resolves #5168 ## Motivation and context Currently, in a Card component, when the `toggles` boolean property is specified: 1. the checkbox that displays on hover or focus does not have an accessibility name. 2. the checkbox cannot receive focus with a keyboard 3. Similarly, in the storybook Grid examples using the Card with an action button, the action button is not keyboard focusable. ## How has this been tested? - [x] _Test case 1_ 1. Go here: https://5168-card-checkbox-a11y--spectrum-wc.netlify.app/storybook/?path=/story/card--toggles 2. Tab into the Storybook story for the Card component with `toggles` boolean property added. 3. First, the Action Menu button should receive keyboard focus, which will fade in the checkbox as well. 4. Press Tab to focus the checkbox. 5. Press Space bar to check the checkbox, which will change the Card state to selected. - [x] _Test case 2_ 1. Go here: https://5168-card-checkbox-a11y--spectrum-wc.netlify.app/storybook/?path=/story/card--default&args=toggles:!true, which is the Default story with the `toggles` control within Storybook set to `true`. 2. Tab into the Storybook story for the Card component with `toggles` boolean property added. 3. First, the checkbox button should receive keyboard focus, which will fade in the checkbox overlay. 5. Press Space bar to check the checkbox, which will change the Card state to selected. - [x] _Test case 3_ 1. Go here: https://5168-card-checkbox-a11y--spectrum-wc.netlify.app/storybook/?path=/story/grid--default 2. Tab into the Storybook story for the Grid component to first focus the text input before the grid containing cards as items. 3. Press Tab again to move focus to the grid. The first card item should receive keyboard focus. 4. Use ArrowDown or ArrowRight to move focus to an adjacent card. 5. Press Tab, which will move focus to the action button within the card, and will fade in the checkbox for to select the Card. 6. Press Tab again to focus the checkbox. 7. Press Space to check the checkbox, which will change the Card state to selected. 8. Press Tab to move focus to the action bar showing selected items and available actions that follows the grid. 9. Press Shift+Tab to move focus back to the grid. The last Card that contained focus should receive focus again. - [x] Did it pass in Desktop? - [ ] Did it pass in Mobile? - [ ] Did it pass in iPad? ## Screenshots (if appropriate) https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3640e420-66b3-4f3f-b4e7-3c4bf789ec95 ## Types of changes - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change) - [ ] Chore (minor updates related to the tooling or maintenance of the repository, does not impact compiled assets) ## Checklist - [x] I have signed the [Adobe Open Source CLA](http://opensource.adobe.com/cla.html). - [x] My code follows the code style of this project. - [x] If my change required a change to the documentation, I have updated the documentation in this pull request. - [x] I have read the **[CONTRIBUTING](<(https://github.com/adobe/spectrum-web-components/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)>)** document. - [x] I have added tests to cover my changes. - [x] All new and existing tests passed. - [x] I have reviewed at the Accessibility Practices for this feature, see: [Aria Practices](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-practices/) ## Best practices This repository uses conventional commit syntax for each commit message; note that the GitHub UI does not use this by default so be cautious when accepting suggested changes. Avoid the "Update branch" button on the pull request and opt instead for rebasing your branch against `main`.

The JS interop design previously described in the overview depended on
the identities of prototypes attached to custom descriptors being
mutable. Implementer feedback from both SpiderMonkey and V8 was that the
identities need to be immutable, so that design was not feasible.

more of our requirements.

# Esqueleto Inicial do Backend com Spring Boot

## Descrição

Este pull request estabelece a base para a parte de backend do projeto, fornecendo um esqueleto com Spring Boot e a estrutura inicial do projeto. As seguintes alterações foram implementadas:

- **Projeto Base com Spring Boot:**
  - Configuração de um novo projeto Spring Boot utilizando o parent starter oficial.
  - Criação da classe principal `ControleEstoquesApplication.java` para inicializar a aplicação.

- **Estrutura do Projeto:**
  - Criação das pastas essenciais para o desenvolvimento futuro:
    - `model`
    - `controller`
    - `dto`
    - `utils`
  - Inclusão de arquivos placeholder (como `.gitkeep`) para manter a estrutura dos diretórios.

- **Arquivos de Build e Configuração:**
  - Adição do arquivo `pom.xml` com as dependências necessárias, incluindo Spring Boot Starter Web, Data JPA, Security e PostgreSQL.
  - Inclusão dos scripts do Maven Wrapper (`mvnw` e `mvnw.cmd`) para padronizar o processo de build.
  - Criação de um arquivo básico `application.properties` com o nome da aplicação configurado.
  - Inclusão do arquivo `HELP.md` contendo documentações e referências sobre Maven, Spring Boot e tecnologias relacionadas.

- **Configuração de Testes:**
  - Adição de um teste básico para verificar se o contexto da aplicação carrega corretamente.

## Commits Incluídos

- `chore(backend): criação da base spring`
- `chore(backend): criação pasta model e controller`
- `chore(backend): criação da pasta utils e dto`

## Considerações Finais

Este esqueleto inicial do backend estabelece a fundação para o desenvolvimento futuro. As alterações atuais focam apenas na criação da estrutura do projeto e na configuração do ambiente base. Em próximos commits, serão adicionadas funcionalidades e regras de negócio conforme a evolução do projeto.

author: davidwrighton
body:
- Convert to the FCALL fast path/QCALL slow path approach
- Make EnterHelperResult/LeaveHelperAction into enum class so that they can safely be silently marshaled between native and managed
- Move the lockTaken flag handling to managed code so we can share more helpers
- Benchmarking indicates that this makes uncontended locks somewhere around 10% faster. I believe this is primarily due to removing a small amount of handling around error checking and lock flag usage which isn't always needed.

### Compression Algorithm Switch:

* [`internal/backend/blob/download.go`](diffhunk://#diff-ea886735d0ee587a3b7ed8bb0cb4b47db450971143af92f56f02e2fde2e4e485L95-R95): Replaced ZSTD with LZ4 for decompression in the `DownloadOutputBlock` function. ### Import Updates:

* [`internal/backend/blob/download.go`](diffhunk://#diff-ea886735d0ee587a3b7ed8bb0cb4b47db450971143af92f56f02e2fde2e4e485L10-R10): Updated import from `github.com/DataDog/zstd` to `github.com/DataDog/golz4`.

body:
This pull request includes several changes to improve the serialization framework by adding support for `std::span`, enhancing type safety, and improving error handling. The most important changes include modifying the `Serializable` class, updating the `JsonObject` class, and adding new serialization functions for `std::span`. Additionally, the test cases have been updated to reflect these changes.

### Serialization Framework Enhancements:

* [`projects/cereal/include/cereal/Cereal.h`](diffhunk://#diff-04a660cb2634457b47edee1d035ba5dfec41b1d573fab12bf919cc311977c41aL42-R42): Modified the `Serialize` method in the `Serializable` class to be non-const, allowing for mutable operations during serialization.

* [`projects/cereal/include/cereal/Json.h`](diffhunk://#diff-bd01530b4e0e9b3937aaf2aed4fd9dc12d303405f6c3a3800be73f534446a73bR32-R114): Added support for `std::span` and type demangling for better error messages. Introduced the `JsonProxy` class to handle type-safe access and assignment of JSON values. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-bd01530b4e0e9b3937aaf2aed4fd9dc12d303405f6c3a3800be73f534446a73bR32-R114) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-bd01530b4e0e9b3937aaf2aed4fd9dc12d303405f6c3a3800be73f534446a73bL63) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-bd01530b4e0e9b3937aaf2aed4fd9dc12d303405f6c3a3800be73f534446a73bL82-R172) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-bd01530b4e0e9b3937aaf2aed4fd9dc12d303405f6c3a3800be73f534446a73bR182-R237)

[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2c1b0aa45e309bec3480f58245c508202e4a11e521890d1ecf77eda7bc2e03eaR34) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2c1b0aa45e309bec3480f58245c508202e4a11e521890d1ecf77eda7bc2e03eaR137-R153) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2c1b0aa45e309bec3480f58245c508202e4a11e521890d1ecf77eda7bc2e03eaR191-R196)

This PR adds support for `FULL OUTER JOIN` queries, which are supported by both Postgres and SQLite (but not MySQL). I'm unaware if there are a specific reason it wasn't originally included, perhaps just as they're not super common, but I've run it to a situation where I do so figured it was worthwhile PRing.

This isn't quite ready, but it has the general structure. It primarily just needs tests and checking that it's done in a good way. Have left a few comments with questions about whether its taking the best approach.

- 레디스를 적용하여 캐싱이 가능하게 처리했습니다
- 카프카에서 오는 데이터를 구독하여 자동으로 검증을 처리할 수 있는 프로세스를 만들었습니다.
- 세금 계산서 데이터를 DB에 저장하는 로직을 구성했습니다

---

---

- application.yml파일 변경으로 인해 실행전 수정이 필요합니다(레디스 관련 업데이트)
- 서버 내에도 업데이트된 docker-compose를 활용하여 레디스 연동을 실시하겠습니다
- 데이터 저장 로직이 서비스에 들어가 있는데 추후 조회 로직 구현시 따로 리포지토리를 구현하여 구현하도록 하겠습니다.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **신규 기능**
	- Redis 클라이언트와 Spring Redis 지원을 추가하여 캐싱 및 데이터 직렬화 성능을 강화했습니다.
	- 세금 계산서 검증 로직을 개선하고, 사용자 인증을 통한 추가 엔드포인트를 도입하여 검증 프로세스를 보완했습니다.
- **리팩토링**
	- 직원 초기화 로직을 개선하여 전화번호 형식을 표준화하고 신규 직원 데이터를 추가했습니다.

	- 세금 계산서 검증 요청 필드의 예시 값을 명확하게 수정했습니다.

This pull request introduces several new checks for practical exercises in various GitHub workflows. These checks aim to validate specific conditions in the code and provide feedback to users. Additionally, there are minor adjustments to permissions and comment update steps.

### New practical exercise checks:

* [`.github/workflows/2-first-introduction.yml`](diffhunk://#diff-63550dfd43bebbf9fe47bf8e7bd129fa58079eb2c5239cd2596fcaa8df392749R72-R115): Added checks to validate the presence of a registration validation comment and additional student activities in `src/app.py`.

| :---: | :---: | :---: | :--: |
| Ready | Feature/Refactor | No |  |

## Problem

1) There was missing blockSubscribe method
2) AccountKeys list in parsed transaction doesn't include writable/readable accounts lists and when you try to get account address by index it might be out of range

## Solution

1) I added support blockSubscribe methods
2) I added special json converter which adds writrable/readable accounts in AccountKeys TransactionMetaInfo parsing stage

## Other changes (e.g. bug fixes, small refactors)
The same JsonSerializerOptions were created many times while compiler recommends to create it just one time
I added default JsonSerializerOptions that can be used at any place

author: nameexhaustion
body: This is a branch with added tracing to await points in the new-streaming compute nodes, intended for finding which await points are blocking execution in the event of a deadlock. Compile and run with `POLARS_TRACED_AWAIT=1` set in the environment, which should print lines to stderr similar to the following: The output should be saved to a file, the following script can then be used to extract the locations at which async tasks are currently blocked: ```python import polars as pl from pathlib import Path trace_file = ".env/trace" df = ( pl.Series("raw", [Path(trace_file).read_text()]) .str.strip_chars_end("\n") .str.split("\n") .list.explode() .to_frame() .filter( pl.first().str.starts_with("begin_await") | pl.first().str.starts_with("finish_await") ) ) v = ( df.with_columns( pl.col("raw") .str.splitn(" ", 3) .struct.rename_fields(["event", "id", "location"]) .struct.unnest() ) .filter(pl.len().over("id") < 2) .unique("location") .sort("location") ) with pl.Config( tbl_formatting="ASCII_MARKDOWN", fmt_str_lengths=999, tbl_width_chars=999, tbl_hide_column_data_types=True, tbl_rows=999, ): print(v.select("location")) ```

author: demoncoder95
body:
We have a race condition when a new metrics-server Pod comes up, between the time that the server updates the node informer cache and it scrapes the nodes in the cache, Karpenter can terminate many nodes at the same time. This leads to the scraper stuck in a loop attempting to connect to the kubelet on terminated/terminating nodes and not progressing from NotReady state for up-to 30mins and we get paged for a kube-system Pod not running. There is no way to configure the `max-retries` to a kubelet, so there is no straight-forward way to configure this in the metrics-server itself.

```go
E0303 15:51:02.423322       1 scraper.go:149] "Failed to scrape node" err="Get \"https://ip-10-151-1-173.eu-central-1.compute.internal:10250/metrics/resource\": dial tcp 10.151.1.173:10250: connect: connection refused" node="ip-10-151-1-173.eu-central-1.compute.internal"
```

This introduces a `startupProbe` on the container where we can have the kubelet kill and restart the container after `2mins` if it's stuck like this, and the restarted Pod should have an updated node informer cache, and proceed to `Ready` state.

# Integrate Client-Side Socket.io for Real-Time Messaging and Chat UI Enhancements

## 📝 Description
This PR introduces client-side implementation of `socket.io` for real-time messaging. It covers message sending, receiving, and displaying within the chat window. The update includes necessary modifications to the context folder, main entry file, and chat UI components.

### 🔧 Changes & Additions
- **Added Client-Side Socket.io Code**
  - Implemented `socket.io-client` setup in the **context folder**.
  - Ensured real-time message sending and receiving functionality.

- **Modified `main.jsx` for Socket.io Integration**
  - Established the socket connection for seamless communication.

- **Implemented Message Sending Functionality**
  - Messages typed in the **message-bar** are now sent via Socket.io.
  
- **Implemented Chat Message Display**
  - Messages are displayed dynamically in the **message-container**.

- **Enhanced `ChatContainer/index.jsx`**
  - Integrated all chat-related components, ensuring proper rendering.

- **Handled Empty Chat UI State**
  - Added logic to render an empty chat page when no messages are available.


## 📌 Additional Notes
- This implementation ensures efficient real-time communication.
- Further improvements can be made to optimize performance and UI.
- Proper error handling and edge case considerations will be addressed in future updates.

  quantity of the product added to the cart.

author: bjrara
body:
## Issue ##
HTTP metric is disabled with the following error message.
`
[otel.javaagent 2025-03-04 19:21:31:397 +0000] [http-nio-8080-exec-1] WARN io.opentelemetry.javaagent.shaded.instrumentation.api.internal.OperationMetricsUtil - Disabling http server metrics because io.opentelemetry.sdk.metrics.SdkDoubleHistogram$SdkDoubleHistogramBuilder does not implement io.opentelemetry.javaagent.shaded.io.opentelemetry.api.incubator.metrics.ExtendedDoubleHistogramBuilder. This prevents using metrics advice, which could result in http server metrics having high cardinality attributes.
`

From the dependency tree, it is introduced by `io.opentelemetry:opentelemetry-exporter-otlp`.
```
|    +--- io.opentelemetry:opentelemetry-exporter-otlp -> 1.44.1
|    |    +--- io.opentelemetry:opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-common:1.44.1
|    |    |    +--- io.opentelemetry:opentelemetry-api-incubator:1.44.1-alpha
|    |    |    \--- io.opentelemetry:opentelemetry-exporter-common:1.44.1
```

The upstream makes it excluded in an distro agent example [here](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/blob/8fcb6b86cbbd3d383e40742369872b569005acd3/examples/distro/agent/build.gradle#L80):
```
// exclude known bootstrap dependencies - they can't appear in the inst/ directory
    dependencies {
      exclude("io.opentelemetry:opentelemetry-api")
      exclude("io.opentelemetry:opentelemetry-context")
      // events API and metrics advice API
      exclude("io.opentelemetry:opentelemetry-api-incubator")
    }
```

## Description of changes: ##
Exclude `opentelemetry-extension-incubator`

Hello. I am planning to use `plthook` library into MetaCall: https://github.com/metacall/core
I was using before `funchook` library but I think this library suits much better to my case.
For this, it requires to support `/DELAYLOAD` import tables, so I extended the code in order to support it.
I wrote a whole proof of concept for demonstrating the case I require: https://github.com/metacall/plthook-poc

I want to share my improvements with the upstream repo. There's also some limitations I have found that I want to share, they are unrelated to this PR but it would be interesting if we can solve them: https://github.com/metacall/plthook-poc?tab=readme-ov-file#limitations

Thanks @kubo for this library!

author: morecache
body:
The "model.set_sort_column_id(4, Gtk.SortType.ASCENDING)" in snapshots.py makes ascend order by column 4(snapshot name column). This patch added a combobox for soring, The default one is descending order by creation time of snapshots, So the latest one is always on the top.

E.g:
root@localhost:~ # virsh snapshot-list --domain tumbleweed
 Name            Creation Time               State
------------------------------------------------------
 desktop_ready   2025-03-03 14:26:23 +0000   running
 paused1         2025-03-03 14:56:57 +0000   paused
 poweroff1       2025-03-03 14:45:17 +0000   shutoff
 snapshot1       2025-03-03 14:23:17 +0000   running
 youtube         2025-03-03 14:42:19 +0000   running

We can see the snapshot list in snapshot page via UI:
 desktop_ready
 paused1
 poweroff1
 snapshot1
 youtube

After the patch, The default order option in the combobox is by creation time, So we can see the snapshot list in snapshot page via UI:
 paused1
 poweroff1
 youtube
 desktop_ready
 snapshot1

Fixes #847

It's sure thing that tree view/tree structure is the best solution, But it take times. 
Here is a simple workaround: A sorting combobox as a short-term solution. Once we got a fully functional tree structure for snapshot UI, We can remove/improve this combobox.

Secure logging endpoints and AJAX interactions with nonce verification, sanitization, and standardized JSON responses

- Updated toggle_logging_callback:
  - Added nonce verification via check_ajax_referer to prevent CSRF.
  - Enforced capability check (current_user_can('manage_options')).
  - Sanitized 'status' input using sanitize_text_field and wp_unslash.
  - Replaced direct echo/json_encode/die with wp_send_json_success/wp_send_json_error for consistent JSON responses.

- Revised jQuery AJAX call:
  - Included nonce field in the POST data (localized via wp_localize_script).
  - Adjusted response handling to access response.data per the updated backend format.

- Enhanced ajax_log endpoint:
  - Sanitized all POST inputs using wp_unslash and sanitize_text_field.
  - Ensured safe logging by strictly processing user inputs.

These changes mitigate CSRF, XSS, and input injection risks, aligning our logging endpoints with best security practices.

<!-- Guidelines: https://docs.spacestation14.io/en/getting-started/pr-guideline -->

## About the PR
Added Pluoxium to the default gas filter list of the Portable Scrubber and SharedVentScrubberComponent.  

## Why / Balance

Introducing anything other than oxygen and nitrogen into Distro goes against the job expectations of an Atmos Tech. Additionally, they are responsible for addressing gas leaks. Given this, it would be reasonable to expect them to also manage Pluoxium leaks. Therefore, I wanted to make dealing with these leaks easier by having it filtered out by default. 

While generally harmless, Pluoxium can cause frustrating pressure imbalances between rooms. Since it is not scrubbed by default, removing it and stabilizing the pressure can be a hassle. Currently, players must manually configure each atmos alarm’s filtering list to manage it, as portable scrubbers cannot assist. The changes I've made address this issue. 

On the plus side, this change makes it easier for players to filter Pluoxium out of the waste pipe network for use.

## Technical details
Added Gas.Pluoxium to the list of filtered gasses in [PortableScrubberComponent.cs](https://github.com/AstroDogeDX/ShibaStation-GS/compare/master...MinxIsntHere:Pluoxium-Bad?expand=1#diff-f535bf303d72cf0be7864a92520ff179c55ed1559e886eafd12661bc21cf35ed) and [SharedVentScrubberComponent.cs](https://github.com/AstroDogeDX/ShibaStation-GS/compare/master...MinxIsntHere:Pluoxium-Bad?expand=1#diff-b606343a83d87af62f19eac5fa08828405cb04fdd7f9b2dd74f058c279025967)

Write a function to delete a directory and all its contents.

## Summary of Changes
Added a new utility function to recursively delete a directory and all of its contents, ensuring thorough and safe directory removal.

## Acceptance Criteria
All tests must pass.

## Tests
 - Verify the function can delete an empty directory
 - Verify the function can delete a directory with nested files and subdirectories
 - Verify the function handles non-existent directories gracefully
 - Verify the function handles permission-related edge cases

body:
**Title**: [Schema] Change `force_delete` Field Type from String to Boolean

**Summary**: Changed the type of `force_delete` field from `String` to `Boolean` across multiple resources to improve type safety and maintain consistency with Terraform best practices. This change affects service, environment, environment group, template, and infrastructure resources.

**Details**:

1. Schema Changes:
   - Modified `force_delete` field type from schema.TypeString to schema.TypeBool
   - Updated helper function from `BuildFieldForBoolean` to `BuildFieldBool` for proper boolean handling
   - Maintained computed and optional attributes

2. Documentation Updates:
   - Updated field type documentation from String to Boolean
   - Improved description clarity for all affected resources
   - Added proper punctuation and consistent formatting
 
3. Test Updates:
   - Added boolean value verification in test cases
   - Maintained `ImportStateVerifyIgnore` for `force_delete` field

4. Affected Resources:
   - Platform Service
   - Platform Environment
   - Platform Environment Group
   - Platform Template
   - Platform Infrastructure

The changes are backward compatible as the previous string values "true"/"false" will be automatically handled by Terraform's type conversion.

**Related Issues:**
[CDS-107596](https://harness.atlassian.net/browse/CDS-107596)

body: ### Description > [!NOTE] > Marius has reviewed and approved of changes Add new menu Items to the menus, in the overview you should show **all the actions** that a user might want to do. The only import is the order. This means that you can schedule an ASAP release if you change your mind without having to actively change the type first. Or from a scheduled release to immediately publish *Overview* - "At a time" releases: Schedule, Run release etc - Other releases: Run release, schedule etc | At a time release | Undecided / ASAP release | | -------- | ------- | | | | *Detail* - "At a time" releases: The schedule release is still main action, Run release etc appears in menu - Other releases: The Run Release is still main action, Schedule release appears in the menu | At a time release | Undecided / ASAP release | | -------- | ------- | | | | All actions moved to menu when release is undecided type - Add Publish and Schedule actions in the dropdown menus - In the overview page and on the release detail footer menu - Reuse existing buttons with dialogues, add new props to allow for this flexibility (`onDialogOpen`, `onDialogClose`, `isMenuItem`) - Refactor menu to use popover instead of tooltip - Add error validations for when no permissions and no documents - Update to the undecided releases to not show a main action ### What to review I've tried to reuse a lot of the existing logic that was already solid. I think I got to a good space without reinventing the wheel and reusing all aspects of what we had, let me know if it's preferable to do it another way ### Testing Updated tests, existing ones should be enough ### Notes for release You can now schedule and publish releases from the release menu.

body:
This pull request introduces several significant changes to the codebase, focusing on the addition of thread pool configurations, enhancements to the `LoginController` and `UserController`, and updates to the `UserService` and `UserMapper`. Below is a summary of the most important changes:

### Thread Pool Configurations:

* Added `CacheThreadPoolConfig` and `NetWorkIOThreadPoolConfig` classes to configure thread pools for cache and network IO operations, respectively. ### Controller Enhancements:

* Updated `LoginController` to use the newly configured thread pools for handling GitHub third-party authentication and Redis operations asynchronously. (`src/main/java/com/what/spring/controller/LoginController.java`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3a20e89e04d235c1dbd0f4fc6e8c3240e3b2bb8189c4214be02764b60a9bf5a2R26-R27) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3a20e89e04d235c1dbd0f4fc6e8c3240e3b2bb8189c4214be02764b60a9bf5a2R43-R48) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-3a20e89e04d235c1dbd0f4fc6e8c3240e3b2bb8189c4214be02764b60a9bf5a2L52-R66) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-3a20e89e04d235c1dbd0f4fc6e8c3240e3b2bb8189c4214be02764b60a9bf5a2R75-R81) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-3a20e89e04d235c1dbd0f4fc6e8c3240e3b2bb8189c4214be02764b60a9bf5a2R100)
* Added `UserController` with a method to retrieve user information using the cache thread pool. (`src/main/java/com/what/spring/controller/UserController.java`)

### Service Enhancements:

* Introduced `UserService` to handle user-related operations, including retrieving user sessions from Redis and fetching raw user information. (`src/main/java/com/what/spring/service/user/UserService.java`)

### Mapper and POJO Updates:

* Updated `UserMapper` to include a method for fetching raw user information by website ID. (`src/main/java/com/what/spring/mapper/UserMapper.java`, `src/main/resources/com/what/spring/mapper/UserMapper.xml`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a937a108542abfc3d5c8f41d12e4c05e1c343e33e6a69b947a522e4a89250056R19-R20) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ec9b584ef1a9d4838e597615b704ad30c9f22ae0aa5934ea6e090b93a1f6ed1eL12-R31)
* Enhanced `Result` and `GithubCallBackResponse` classes to support additional fields and methods. (`src/main/java/com/what/spring/pojo/Result.java`, `src/main/java/com/what/spring/pojo/thirAuth/GithubCallBackResponse.java`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-88687213dd76bb14ab0d6280398cc6d6174df94e854de077b13757bba8210af5R12-R18) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-9062657a6d7de651e87a81893afbf97f8c09f9ef18c436afaa86410ced2c688eR9)

### Configuration Updates:

* Updated `application.yaml` to include configurations for the new thread pools and modified frontend URLs. (`src/main/resources/application.yaml`)

These changes collectively improve the application's performance by leveraging thread pools for asynchronous operations and enhance user-related functionalities.

- Webhooks implemented
  - Initially sms status handled by existing logic

  - Max Retry is kept at 0 - means if fails to send notification won’t retry & skip.
  - On failed notification, method.failCount will be +1 & upon reaching a threshold method will be disabled.

### Explanation of Change

Design doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1prFcvgUlEGRuL3zE-JH-lhv_BWX2lL2YNw61w4YVnyY/edit?tab=t.0

This PR expands the Help Pane by adding initial content for key sections and ensuring users always see relevant information.

#### **Key Changes:**  
- **Contextual Help Content**: Implemented a **content map** to show help content based on the current route, falling back to the closest parent if none is available.  
- **Initial Content Added**: Covers `/r`, `/search`, `/settings`, `/settings/workspaces`, and `/settings/workspaces/:policyID`.  
- **Handling Missing Content**:  
  - On **staging**, missing content shows diagnostic info.  
  - On **production**, the parent page content remains visible instead of an empty panel. 
- **Testing & Deployment**: Button visibility is still controlled via NVP on production, and all logic remains client-side (no backend integration yet).

    Onyx.set('nvp_sidePane', {})

## Context

Following an internal accessibility audit, some improvements to visually hidden link text were identified.

## Changes proposed in this pull request

- `CandidateInterface::CompleteSectionComponent` submit visually hidden link text has changed from "Continue" → "Save changes and return to your details"
- An aria label was used to achieve this as `content_tag` caused the screen reader to repeat the text twice
- The 'back' visually hidden link text on the referee personal email address interruption page has changed from "Back" → "Go back and change the email address"
- A custom back link with the relevant CSS classes was used in the personal email address interruption view to achieve the custom aria-label as the `GovukComponent::BackLinkComponent` could not be easily altered to accept an aria value

## Guidance to review

- Log in as a candidate user.
- Please review a sample of the affected pages (QA links below):
- [ ] Several completed sections linking from the ['Your details' page](https://qa.apply-for-teacher-training.service.gov.uk/candidate/application/details) which ought to contain the `CandidateInterface::CompleteSectionComponent`component
- [ ] Click 'Add Reference' and enter a personal email address when [adding a referee](https://qa.apply-for-teacher-training.service.gov.uk/candidate/application/references/review), e.g. `example@gmail.com`, and review the resulting interruption page with screen reader enabled

# Implement Knight's Tour Solver with Backtracking Algorithm

## Task
Create a program that solves the Knight's Tour problem on an 8x8 chessboard. The program must find a sequence of knight moves that visits every square exactly once, starting from a given initial position.

## Acceptance Criteria
All tests must pass. The program must create an 8x8 chessboard representation. The knight must move according to standard chess knight movement rules. Every square must be visited exactly once. A backtracking algorithm must be used to explore possible tours. If no valid tour is found, the program must indicate this.

## Summary of Changes
Implemented a Knight's Tour solver using a backtracking algorithm. The solution includes:
- An 8x8 chessboard representation
- Knight movement validation
- Backtracking algorithm to explore all possible tour sequences
- Handling for cases where no valid tour exists
- Comprehensive test suite to verify solution correctness

## Test Cases
 - Verify knight movement follows standard chess rules
 - Confirm chessboard is 8x8 in dimensions
 - Check that every square is visited exactly once
 - Test backtracking algorithm finds a complete tour
 - Validate handling of impossible tour scenarios
 - Ensure starting position can be configured
 - Verify solution works for different initial knight positions
 - Check performance and efficiency of backtracking approach

author: 1abhishekpandey
body:
# Description

- Here's how we give the preference: `externalId` vs. `userId`
    - If current `externalId` is not nil, and either `previousExternalId` is nil or, if present, it is not equal to the current externalId, then set the current externalId.
    - If current externalId is nil then repeat the above process for the userId.
- Fixed the issue where we were setting `nil`, if externalId is nil.
- Fixed the issue where, if in the same app run, more than one identify event is made with the same userId but with different externalId, then we need to set the new externalId to Braze. Previously, in this case, only the first externalId was being set.
    - This issue was occurring because we are not creating a deep copy of the message object, specifically the `externalId`. Now, as a workaround, we're directly caching the `brazeExternalId` value; instead of relying on the cached message object. 
    - We tested the userId and other traits value and they are being set properly.
- ~~Fixed duplication symbol issue. We reverted the import header changes that we did in the last PR.~~ In Factory classes, we have to change the import from `#import <Rudder/Rudder.h>` to the following code: This is required to address the build failure when this package is integrated using SPM. In case, if we don't add this then there will be build failure.
```
#if defined(__has_include) && __has_include(<Rudder/Rudder.h>)
#import <Rudder/Rudder.h>
#else
#import "Rudder.h"
#endif
```

# Breaking change

- Previously, if in the same app run, more than one identify event is made with the same userId but with different externalId, then only the first externalId was being set.
- Now, in such scenarios, we are setting the updated (or changed) externalId.

author: noredeen
body:
The goal of this PR was to get the VSCode Go language client to work. In this pursuit, some significant changes were made:

* The introduction of `lspwatch` modes: `command` and `proxy`. The correct mode is automatically detected but there are options to set explicitly.

* Dropping `textproto.Reader` in favour of manual header parsing. The existing message parsing setup is buggy in very subtle ways and I don't have time for this whac-a-mole involving 3+ nested readers.

* Stability improvements. Reading EOF causes `lspwatch` to exit.

* Stderr of the language server process now captures in logs.

* Fix broken exit codes.

And now `lspwatch` works reliably in VSCode!

body:
### PR Description:
This pull request introduces key features focused on improving asset security, ownership validation, and advanced asset management functionalities. Changes include:

- **Ownership and Security Features**:
  - `verify-asset-ownership`: Validates if a claimed owner matches the actual owner of an asset.
  - `retrieve-ownership-records`: Fetches the ownership records for a specific asset, providing better traceability.
  - `get-validated-metadata`: Retrieves validated metadata for an asset.
  - `validate-transfer-security`: Ensures security during asset transfers by verifying ownership and asset status.
  - `security-verification`: Verifies that an asset is not destroyed and its metadata exists before performing critical operations.

- **Advanced Asset Management**:
  - `validate-metadata-batch`: Validates a batch of metadata URLs for bulk creation, ensuring compliance with batch size limits.
  - `check-batch-status`: Retrieves the creation status of a specific batch, adding visibility into the batch processing workflow.
  - `asset-extended-info`: Stores extended details such as creation timestamp and properties for each asset, improving asset metadata tracking.
  - `get-asset-extended-info`: Fetches additional details about an asset, providing more in-depth information.
  
- **System Monitoring and Performance**:
  - `contract-monitoring`: A map that stores system-wide monitoring data, such as total assets and maximum allowed batch size.
  - `get-system-limits`: Exposes contract limits like the maximum bulk size for creation and metadata length, offering better system insights.

These improvements enhance asset tracking, ownership validation, security during transfers, and system monitoring capabilities, providing stronger governance and better control over asset data.

author: wenfengye
body:
It has been a mess, but I believe I can draw some final conclusions.

Generally, incompressibility must be carefully managed to avoid numerical issues. If Poisson's ratio (nu) is too high (nu > 0.4999), the stiffness matrix becomes ill-conditioned, which can lead to convergence problems. On the other hand, if nu < 0.49, LS-DYNA will issue a warning, and the assumption of nearly incompressibility for hyperelastic materials no longer holds,  it can also lead to divergence.

In past, nu is set constaly to 0.499, it leads to a bulk modulus (kappa) close to 1 MPa with a template passive material (k1 = 0.00236),  which works well. However, with the Gulektin material where k1 = 0.0004, the resulting kappa=0.2 is too low and never converged. Based on my recent tests with the Gulektin material, the simulation converges well when kappa is greater than or equal to 0.4 (nu > 0.4995). However, this is not a definitive conclusion, as the stiffness of the fibers from the anisotropic part also influences the results, making the situation quite complex.
Moreover, a high value of kappa can lead to increased oscillations (as observed in the control volume pressure), even if the simulation has converged. A kappa to shear modulus ratio of 100 appears to be recommended.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/082f41a8-c905-476e-af67-1fb33ad8cc4a).

Regarding the isotropic stiff (Neo-Hookean) parts used for the stiff base, aorta... kappa of 1 MPa is too low compared to the shear modulus (mu) of 0.1 MPa, which also leads to divergence. A more balanced choice is kappa = 10 MPa, as updated in this pull request.

That said, the situation isn't entirely resolved. ETYPE=13 typically suggests using the same kappa for connected parts, but we’re currently deviating from that guideline. One solution is to replace the these parts with ETYPE=10 by neglecting locking issue on these parts, which could be explored in the future if necessary. However, based on my current testing, the existing settings seem to work fine, and this change does not offer significant improvements.

body:
### Update [tensorflow](https://pypi.org/project/tensorflow) from **1.15.4** to **2.18.0**.


<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 2.18.0
   ```
   TensorFlow

 Breaking Changes

* `tf.lite`
    * C API:
      * An optional, fourth parameter was added `TfLiteOperatorCreate` as a step forward towards a cleaner API for `TfLiteOperator`. Function `TfLiteOperatorCreate` was added recently, in TensorFlow Lite version 2.17.0, released on 7/11/2024, and we do not expect there will be much code using this function yet. Any code breakages can be easily resolved by passing nullptr as the new, 4th parameter.

* TensorRT support is disabled in CUDA builds for code health improvement.

* TensorFlow now supports and is compiled with NumPy 2.0 by default. Please see the [NumPy 2 release notes](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/release/2.0.0-notes.html) and the [NumPy 2 migration guide](https://numpy.org/devdocs/numpy_2_0_migration_guide.html#numpy-2-migration-guide).
  * Note that NumPy's type promotion rules have been changed(See [NEP 50](https://numpy.org/neps/nep-0050-scalar-promotion.html#nep50)for details). This may change the precision at which computations happen, leading either to type errors or to numerical changes to results.
  * Tensorflow will continue to support NumPy 1.26 until 2025, aligning with community standard deprecation timeline [here](https://scientific-python.org/specs/spec-0000/).

* Hermetic CUDA support is added.

  Hermetic CUDA uses a specific downloadable version of CUDA instead of the user’s locally installed CUDA. Bazel will download CUDA, CUDNN and NCCL distributions, and then use CUDA libraries and tools as dependencies in various Bazel targets. This enables more reproducible builds for Google ML projects and supported CUDA versions.

* Remove the `EnumNamesXNNPackFlags` function in `tensorflow/lite/acceleration/configuration/configuration_generated.h`.

  This change is a bug fix in the automatically generated code. This change is automatically generated by the new flatbuffer generator. The flatbuffers library is updated to 24.3.25 in https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/commit/c17d64df85a83c1bd0fd7dcc0b1230812b0d3d48. The new flatbuffers library includes the following change https://github.com/google/flatbuffers/pull/7813 which fixed a underlying flatbuffer code generator bug.


 Known Caveats

 Major Features and Improvements

*   `tf.lite`:
    *   The LiteRT [repo](https://github.com/google-ai-edge/LiteRT) is live (see [announcement](https://developers.googleblog.com/en/tensorflow-lite-is-now-litert/)), which means that in the coming months there will be changes to the development experience for TFLite. The TF Lite Runtime source will be moved later this year, and sometime after that we will start accepting contributions through that repo.
    *   SignatureRunner is now supported for models with no signatures.

 Bug Fixes and Other Changes

* `tf.data`
    * Add optional `synchronous` argument to `map`, to specify that the `map` should run synchronously, as opposed to be parallelizable when `options.experimental_optimization.map_parallelization=True`. This saves memory compared to setting `num_parallel_calls=1`.
    * Add optional `use_unbounded_threadpool` argument to `map`, to specify that the `map` should use an unbounded threadpool instead of the default pool that is based on the number of cores on the machine. This can improve throughput for map functions which perform IO or otherwise release the CPU.
    * Add [`tf.data.experimental.get_model_proto`](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/data/experimental/get_model_proto) to allow users to peek into the analytical model inside of a dataset iterator.

* `tf.lite`
    * `Dequantize` op supports `TensorType_INT4`.
        * This change includes per-channel dequantization.
    * Add support for `stablehlo.composite`.
    * `EmbeddingLookup` op supports per-channel quantization and `TensorType_INT4` values.
    * `FullyConnected` op supports `TensorType_INT16` activation and `TensorType_Int4` weight per-channel quantization.
    * Enable per-tensor quantization support in dynamic range quantization of `TRANSPOSE_CONV` layer. Fixes TFLite converter [bug](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/issues/76624).

* `tf.tensor_scatter_update`, `tf.tensor_scatter_add` and of other reduce types.
    * Support `bad_indices_policy`.

 Thanks to our Contributors

This release contains contributions from many people at Google, as well as:

Akhil Goel, akhilgoe, Alexander Pivovarov, Amir Samani, Andrew Goodbody, Andrey Portnoy, Anthony Platanios, bernardoArcari, Brett Taylor, buptzyb, Chao, Christian Clauss, Cocoa, Daniil Kutz, Darya Parygina, dependabot[bot], Dimitris Vardoulakis, Dragan Mladjenovic, Elfie Guo, eukub, Faijul Amin, flyingcat, Frédéric Bastien, ganyu.08, Georg Stefan Schmid, Grigory Reznikov, Harsha H S, Harshit Monish, Heiner, Ilia Sergachev, Jan, Jane Liu, Jaroslav Sevcik, Kaixi Hou, Kanvi Khanna, Kristof Maar, Kristóf Maár, LakshmiKalaKadali, Lbertho-Gpsw, lingzhi98, MarcoFalke, Masahiro Hiramori, Mmakevic-Amd, mraunak, Nobuo Tsukamoto, Notheisz57, Olli Lupton, Pearu Peterson, pemeliya, Peyara Nando, Philipp Hack, Phuong Nguyen, Pol Dellaiera, Rahul Batra, Ruturaj Vaidya, sachinmuradi, Sergey Kozub, Shanbin Ke, Sheng Yang, shengyu, Shraiysh, Shu Wang, Surya, sushreebarsa, Swatheesh-Mcw, syzygial, Tai Ly, terryysun, tilakrayal, Tj Xu, Trevor Morris, Tzung-Han Juang, wenchenvincent, wondertx, Xuefei Jiang, Ye Huang, Yimei Sun, Yunlong Liu, Zahid Iqbal, Zhan Lu, Zoranjovanovic-Ns, Zuri Obozuwa
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.17.1
   ```
   Bug Fixes and Other Changes

* Add necessary header files in the aar library. These are needed if developers build apps with header files unpacked from tflite aar files from maven.
* Implement Name() for GCSWritableFile to fix the profiler trace viewer cache file generation.
* Fix `cstring.h` missing file issue with the Libtensorflow archive.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.17.0
   ```
   TensorFlow

 Breaking Changes

* GPU
    * Support for NVIDIA GPUs with compute capability 5.x (Maxwell generation) has been removed from TF binary distributions (Python wheels).

 Major Features and Improvements

*   Add `is_cpu_target_available`, which indicates whether or not TensorFlow was built with support for a given CPU target. This can be useful for skipping target-specific tests if a target is not supported.

*   `tf.data`
    * Support `data.experimental.distribued_save`. `distribued_save` uses tf.data service (https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/data/experimental/service) to write distributed dataset snapshots. The call is non-blocking and returns without waiting for the snapshot to finish. Setting `wait=True` to `tf.data.Dataset.load` allows the snapshots to be read while they are being written.

 Bug Fixes and Other Changes

* GPU
    * Support for NVIDIA GPUs with compute capability 8.9 (e.g. L4 & L40) has been added to TF binary distributions (Python wheels).
* Replace `DebuggerOptions` of TensorFlow Quantizer, and migrate to `DebuggerConfig` of StableHLO Quantizer.
* Add TensorFlow to StableHLO converter to TensorFlow pip package.
* TensorRT support: this is the last release supporting TensorRT. It will be removed in the next release.
* NumPy 2.0 support: TensorFlow is going to support NumPy 2.0 in the next release. It may break some edge cases of TensorFlow API usage.

* `tf.lite`
    * Quantization for `FullyConnected` layer is switched from per-tensor to per-channel scales for dynamic range quantization use case (`float32` inputs / outputs and `int8` weights). The change enables new quantization schema globally in the converter and inference engine. The new behaviour can be disabled via experimental flag `converter._experimental_disable_per_channel_quantization_for_dense_layers = True`.
    * C API:
        * The experimental `TfLiteRegistrationExternal` type has been renamed as `TfLiteOperator`

author: davidspickett
body:
When https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/130034 enabled RISC-V here I noticed that these should run for ARM as well.

ARM only has 4 argument registers, which matches Arm's ABI for it: https://github.com/ARM-software/abi-aa/blob/main/aapcs32/aapcs32.rst#core-registers

The ABI defines a link register LR, and I assume that's what becomes 'ra' in LLDB.

Tested on ARM and AArch64 Linux.

This pull request introduces several significant changes to the `Sarah.Server` project, including the addition of new services, updates to configuration files, and modifications to existing classes to integrate the new services. The key changes are summarized below:

### Service Integration and Initialization:

* Added `IEventProcessingService` and `IMonitoringService` to the service collection in `AddSarahServices` method and created a new `InitSarahServices` method to initialize these services (`Sarah.Server/Extensions/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d7ff93400b2a567632ddc20954365690ed45a621ad4211b385c168c5f70d0e52R24) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d7ff93400b2a567632ddc20954365690ed45a621ad4211b385c168c5f70d0e52R33-R55)
* Updated `Program.cs` to use the new `InitSarahServices` method for initializing services (`Sarah.Server/Program.cs`).

### Configuration Updates:

* Added new configuration sections for `RabbitMQ`, `OpenWeatherMap`, `iCalFolder`, and `WeatherWarnLocation` in `appsettings.json` (`Sarah.Server/appsettings.json`).

### Project and Solution File Modifications:

* Included new project references for `Sarah.EventProcessing` and `Sarah.Monitoring` in `Sarah.Server.csproj` and updated the solution file to include these projects (`Sarah.Server/Sarah.Server.csproj`, `Sarah.sln`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b86f409ae05368bcb916c4e1bfa8ad8b0962341bf77fb66db40f4a6d1abf5330R39-R40) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-62d3d92dcce8e12fdce348f33d047ba69c409ad7f1d51735c4b22c1bc88d9417R26-R29)

* Refactored `NetworkElement` class to use `IEventProcessingService` for event reporting instead of `NetworkEventAggregator` (`Services/Sarah.API/BusinessObjects/NetworkElement.cs`).

[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a7cf4c8e5e857e966c8d3aa9683f40d076d42fddfd49b3b7fd7f042c3d0ebc9bL12-R28) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a7cf4c8e5e857e966c8d3aa9683f40d076d42fddfd49b3b7fd7f042c3d0ebc9bR41-R42)

These changes collectively enhance the functionality and maintainability of the `Sarah.Server` project by integrating new services and improving the existing code structure.

body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/austenstone/github-value/security/code-scanning/1186](https://github.com/austenstone/github-value/security/code-scanning/1186)

To fix the problem, we need to parse the URL and check the host value explicitly. This ensures that the check handles arbitrary subdomain sequences correctly and prevents bypassing the check by embedding 'smee.io' in unexpected locations.

- Parse the URL using the `URL` constructor to extract the host.
- Check if the host is exactly 'smee.io' or one of its subdomains.
- Update the condition on line 36 to use this parsed host value.

author: paultranvan
body:
This includes improvements to improve queries performances, after we noticed a high cozy-client overhead on large queries.
The details and performances improvements can be found in dedicated commits. 

For an overall performance insight, we measured a big query retrieving 25K documents, on a Redmi Note 10 mobile.
The query is the following: `await client.query(Q('io.cozy.files').limitBy(null))`

The results are : 

Before: 
- 2328ms to read pouch data 
**- Total: 5303ms**
- **43%** of total time is spent on database side

After:
- 2749ms to read pouch data
**- Total: 3156ms**
- **87%** of total time is spent on database side

Thus, before, 57% of the total query time was spent *outside* of the database. Now it is only 13% :rocket:

# Added `CartItemLocator` for Dynamic Furniture Search & Addition to Cart

## Summary
This PR introduces the `CartItemLocator` class, which allows users to add furniture to their shopping cart based on attributes rather than specific IDs.

## Features Implemented:
- **Furniture Type Mapping:** Supports searching for chairs, tables, sofas, beds, and bookcases.
- **Attribute-Based Search:** Finds furniture based on color, material, size, and other attributes.
- **Inventory Validation:** Ensures items are available in stock before adding them to the cart.
- **Error Handling:** Raises appropriate errors for unknown furniture types, missing attributes, and insufficient stock.

## Additional Changes:
- **Added Unit Tests:** Implemented `test_cart_item_locator.py` using `unittest.mock` to validate all core functionalities.

## Next Steps:
- Integrate `CartItemLocator` into the checkout and order flow.


Please review and provide feedback.

body:
Audit feedback indicated that deleting state prior to handling transfers could allow solvers to trigger `reject` and `markFulfilled` on their own orders. They don't gain any material advantage from this, but it would cause the contracts to emit confusing logs. Fixed this by applying state transitions first, transfers second, and state purges last.

author: stylie777
body:
Previously, the use of MVE or MVE.FP would be defined by using the `ARM::AEK_SIMD` identifier. SIMD relates to the Cortex-A and Cortex-R extension that enables NEON instructions, which is called MVE for Cortex-M. To enable the linking of `+simd` and `+nosimd` to `+neon` and `-neon` when using clang, MVE and MVE.FP is now be defined using a unique enum identifier, rather than using the existing identifier for SIMD.


This patch is not changing behaviour, rather the enum value used to identify the use of MVE or MVE.FP. The only tests that require updating is the unit tests related to the AEK values themselves.

body:
# logger-f v2.1.5
## [2.1.5](https://github.com/Kevin-Lee/logger-f/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed+milestone%3Av2-m1-11) - 2025-03-08

## Done
* [`logger-f-logback-mdc-monix3`] Bump `logback-scala-interop` to `1.5.0` and `logback` to `1.5.5` (#570)

  Since `logback` `1.5.1`, `LoggerContext.setMDCAdapter` allows setting the inner `mdcAdapter: MDCAdapter` more than once. Previously, assigning a new `mdcAdapter` only worked when `mdcAdapter` was `null`.
  
  So, `LoggerContext.setMDCAdapter` is used instead of reflection to set `Monix3MdcAdapter` as `LoggerContext`'s `mdcAdapter`.

author: matheuscscp
body:
This PR introduces a token cache in source-controller. At the moment, we use it for GitHub App tokens in the `GitRepository` API.

This token cache will report the following metrics:

* Counter `gotk_token_cache_events_total`
  * Help: `Total number of cache retrieval events for a Gitops Toolkit resource reconciliation.`
  * Labels: `event_type`, `kind`, `name`, `namespace`. The values of `event_type` can be `cache_miss` or `cache_hit`.
* Counter `gotk_token_cache_requests_total`
  * Help: `Total number of cache requests partioned by success or failure.`
  * Labels: `status`. The values of `status` can be `success` or `failure`.
* Counter `gotk_token_cache_evictions_total`
  * Help: `Total number of cache evictions.`
  * No labels.
* Gauge `gotk_token_cached_items`
  * Help: `Total number of items in the cache.`
  * No labels.

Versions

Steps

Issue
-----
The ribbon element is technically always visible, even if the product has no ribbon. This can lead to CSS shadow being applied to it, resulting in a white triangle in the top right corner of images: 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d301bd93-7d3e-49e2-848d-c1551b54e3cf)

Cause
-----
The `_get_position_class` method returns a position, even for empty recordsets, in which case it will return `o_ribbon_right`.

Solution

If there is no record, return the `d-none` class to properly hide the element.

# Test Naming Guidelines Update

Updates our test naming conventions to improve clarity and maintainability of our test suite.

## Key Changes

- Established clear guidelines for naming unit tests
- Added examples of good and bad practices
- Introduced principles for more descriptive and concise test names

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Documentation-only changes to contributor guidelines; no runtime, security, or application code is affected.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Updates `docs/testing/unit-testing.md`** with clearer, more prescriptive guidance on how to name and structure unit tests, plus editorial tightening across the rest of the page.
> 
> The **`it` description** section is the main addition: eight numbered rules (present-tense verbs, outcome-focused wording, no filler like "should", avoid implementation details, etc.) and many new 🚫/✅ example pairs (tokens, redirects, errors, vague names). Snapshot tests now recommend names like **`matches rendered snapshot`** instead of **`should renders correctly`**, with complete example blocks.
> 
> Other sections are largely **reworded for brevity** (Jest intro, `describe` grouping, four-phase tests, isolation, `beforeEach` vs helpers, mocks, snapshots). Minor structural tweaks include bullet lists for private-code types, dropping the 💡 prefix on one heading, and removing one "Read more" link under test-as-specification.

author: yuxincs
body:
We added handling for `iter.Seq` and `iter.Seq2` in NilAway such that at least it does not crash (though we assume the return values are always non-nil until better support is added). 

However, Go 1.23 actually introduces more powerful iter-over-func feature, where any of the following func types can be used in range statement:

```
func(func() bool)
func(func(K) bool)
func(func(K, V) bool)
```

and `iter.Seq` and `iter.Seq2` are simply generic type wrapper around the second and third type.

This PR adds general handling for iter-over-func feature (in the same manner: we assume the return values are nonnil). Moreover, we added a `util/typeshelper` package to host our own utility library for `types` package. 

We should be migrating some of the functions from `util` to `tyepshelper`, but that can be done in follow-up PRs.

author: fw-bot
body:
### Steps to reproduce:
- Create a new invoice
- Attach a ZIP file then a PDF file
- The file viewer shows but tries to preview the ZIP file
- Happens with all non-viewable files

### Cause:
The ZIP file is put as main attachment and the method `register_as_main_attachment` only change the main attachment (with `force=False`) when there is no main attachment.

The behavior of the file viewer is problematic because we cannot switch between the attachments in the preview, so we cannot see the PDF. But if we add another PDF file (so one ZIP and 2 PDFs), we can switch but it will never show the ZIP again, only the two PDFs. This behavior is due to the [next/previous arrows](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/e4da068d6c9c8885dd4663d50dee11c9ea1516a3/addons/mail/static/src/components/web_client_view_attachment_view/web_client_view_attachment_view.xml#L13) being displayed only if [`attachmentsInWebClientView`](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/e4da068d6c9c8885dd4663d50dee11c9ea1516a3/addons/mail/static/src/models/attachment.js#L323-L328) contains more than one item. But this list only contains viewable attachments (PDF or Images), and the next/previous arrows only take attachments from this list. As the arrows are [changing the main attachment](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/e4da068d6c9c8885dd4663d50dee11c9ea1516a3/addons/mail/static/src/models/web_client_view_attachment_view.js#L17) to change the displayed preview, it never comes back to the problematic ZIP file.

### Solution:
Also display the arrows if the main attachment is not viewable and there is more than one attachment.
This way the user can return in the list of viewable attachments.

This is not an optimal because Odoo will still try to display the ZIP file, but it is a simple fix that works. 
I tried restraining the main attachment field only to viewable files in this [PR](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/pull/196390), but it seems to break things specially with OCR extraction and apparently it is sometimes wanted to have an XML as main attachment.

Fixes rdar://146459104.

author: bbendou
body:
This PR introduces the initial implementation of FastAPI backend endpoints into the main backend branch. While the core structure and endpoints are functional, further improvements and refinements may be needed as development progresses.

**Key Changes:**

1. Introduced a Layered Architecture
- Repository Layer (repository/) → Handles raw database queries.
- Service Layer (services/) → Implements business logic and processes API responses.
- Router Layer (routers/) → Defines FastAPI endpoints and connects to the service layer.

2. Implemented Core API Endpoints
- GET /courses/{course_code} → Fetch a course by its code.
- GET /courses?department=XX → Retrieve courses within a department.
- GET /courses/filter → Fetch courses by major-specific requirements (CS, IS, BA, BS).

3. Database & Query Handling
-  Refactored db.py to focus on session management (SessionLocal, get_db()).
- Improved Query Logic: Enforced AND filtering for /courses/filter to ensure courses meet all specified requirements.
- Ensured query stability for department-based and course-based searches.

author: twomice
body:
Compared with #65, this fix gets more to the heart of the matter, which is this:

The extension (as of current `master` branch) is doing _extra unnecessary work_:

A. In the buildForm hook, it aims to set the 'percentage' checkbox "price/amount" to "0" (this is the buggy part as of current CiviCRM versions.)
B. Then, in `public_price_set_form.js` it does some manual work to subtract the checkbox amount from the calculated total, when the appropriate payment method is selected (in the case of #64, that means "pay later").  This is actually not needed, if the buildForm hook were doing its job and setting the checkbox price to "0".

This PR does 2 things:
1. Correct the bug mentioned in "A".
2. Remove the redundant/needless "subtract 0 from total" logic in the JS, mentioend in "B".

**More on the bug in "A":**

- Older CiviCRM versions set a 'price' attribute on checkbox fields like `["30","20||"]`
- Newer civicrm versions set that same attribute like `[30,"20||"]` (not the missing double-quotes around `30`.
- As a result, the regex in the buildForm hook was not making the required changes.
- This PR corrects that regex by expecting the double-quotes around the first value (e.g. `30`) to be optional.

author: pmilenkovictt
body:
### Ticket
#18528

### Problem description
The Blackhole did not have the narrow row feature implementation, causing ResNet-50 fold test to fail. 

### What's changed
The additions include the pack_untilize API change, enabling the narrow_row parameter that was unused up to this point to be passed to the LLK.
The LLK additions modify the untilize algorithm for the packer, in order to disable the reads from Face 1 and Face 3 and only allow the reads from F0 and F2 when the narrow_row is set to true.

author: mikrz
body:
When a TTY is not available, or otherwise $TERM is set to `dumb`, returning 1 can cause the calling application to assume actual failure, potentially interfering with regular function. Returning 0 may be a bit less clear about zsh-eza's failure, but it doesn't misrepresent the state of the shell otherwise.

Printing a message will still communicate that the shell did not load zsh-eza in those cases where the user is trying to figure out where the issue lies.

An example of this problem is XPipe, where it's background non-tty enabled session fails to load, as it believes ZSH is failing to start.

author: zulissimeta
body:
## Summary of Changes

`lru_cache` is used to make sure that each MLP calculator is only instantiated once (great!). However, if you want to pass dictionaries through to the underlying calculator (say, config overrides to the fairchem calculator), you will get errors because dictionaries are mutable and lru_cache is unhappy. We can patch this by converting any dictionary kwargs to a frozendict.

author: gaojude
body:
Some analytics APIs need to run before any Next.js code executes. Previously, we implemented `instrumentation.ts` to handle this on the server side. When placed at the project root, this script will be bundled into the initial JavaScript chunk and executed synchronously before hydration begins.

Closes NDX-934

author: matthew-carroll
body:
[SuperEditor] - Keyboard safe area: Catch possible local to global exception.

Apparently, under some circumstances, when we try to run local-to-global within the keyboard safe area, it can happen when some number of ancestors have a dirty layout, which then throws an exception.

This PR catches that exception and returns zero.

It's unclear what specific situation is causing this. When I ran into this in a client app, I think the specific offending widget was a fractional translation box, or something similar. But it's not clear why it was in a dirty layout state.

author: david-josue-murillo
body:
This pull request introduces significant improvements and new implementations in the system's backend. The primary goal is to enhance the structure of the District entity's service layer while also improving the management of the UserEntity by applying best practices in dependency injection and data transfer object (DTO) usage.

**Changes Included in This PR**

1. Implementation of District Services

    - A new service layer (DistrictService) has been created to handle business logic related to District entities.

    - A corresponding REST controller (DistrictController) has been implemented to expose endpoints for district management.
    - DTOs (DistrictRequest and DistrictResponse) have been introduced to ensure that the API does not expose internal JPA entities directly.

2. Refactor of UserEntity Management

    - The UserEntityController now utilizes a DTO (UserRequest) to improve data handling and ensure better separation between the database model and the API layer.

    - Some unnecessary validations related to UserEntity have been removed to simplify the code.

3. Improvements in Dependency Injection

    - Constructor-based dependency injection has been applied using @RequiredArgsConstructor, which improves maintainability and testability.

4. Code Optimization

    - Redundant lines of code have been removed to enhance readability and maintainability.

5. Update and Creation of Unit Tests

    - Unit tests for DistrictController have been created to validate the new implementations.

    - Existing tests have been modified to align with the recent changes in the UserEntity structure.

How to Test the Changes

1. Start the application and test the District API endpoints using Postman or any API testing tool.
2. Verify that responses correctly return DTOs instead of exposing JPA entities.
3. Run the unit tests using Maven (mvn test) to confirm that all tests pass successfully.

## Summary

Updates the plugin PVP spec to include the `Configure` method and the ability for plugin to specific their configuration options via the plugin manifest. The `Configure` method is only called on a plugin that has options specified in the manifest. This also include documentation updates for creating new plugins.

## Rationale 

The `Configure` method is called after the plugin is launched and before it is returned in the `PluginManager` to ensure the plugin has all necessary configuration data to perform transformations.

This replicates the `PluginConfig` in [compliance-to-policy ](https://github.com/oscal-compass/compliance-to-policy/blob/56a48a1727d2718f538d3619a8c7a18ac445aea6/plugins_public/plugins/auditree.py#L49) and allows the data to be passed to the plugins. author: haacked
body:
## Problem

@havenbarnes noticed the following exception in our logs:

> File \"/code/posthog/api/decide.py\", line 318, in get_decide\n    response.update(flags_response)\nValueError: dictionary update sequence element #0 has length 117; 2 is required"}

This bug was introduced in this commit: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/commit/d20ab4521bbcb6b3c5592859930b9b548c04608c

The root issue is that the `get_decide` method would return a cors_response early if `distinct_id` was not in the request data. However, the logic for evaluating feature flags was moved into the `get_feature_flag_response` method. That method usually returns a `dict`, but if `distinct_id` was not in the request, it would still return a `cors_response`. This caused the issue when we later tried to call `response.update(flags_response)` which expects a dictionary but got an `HttpResponse`.

## Changes

I tried to make the minimal changes:

1. Rename `get_feature_flags_response` to `get_feature_flags_response_or_body` for clarity and add type hint that it can return `dict | HttpResponse`.
2. In `get_decide`, if we get an `HttpResponse` from `get_feature_flags_response_or_body`, return it.
3. Also added some more type hints. Type hints would have caught this issue earlier.

## Does this work well for both Cloud and self-hosted?

Yes

## How did you test this code?

Ran unit tests.
Added new failing unit test that now passes.
Manual testing using Postman.

Addresses: #72816
This works by assigning files from the file iterator to specific replicas. 
This PR also implements task stealing, so that if a replica is not available or is slow, other replicas will process its tasks. In terms of filesystem cache locality, though, this means that at the end of iterating through tasks, some task stealing is inevitable, preventing us from achieving perfect cache locality. ~~I've added a 50ms sleep before the stealing is allowed to proceed, which helps a bit, but I'm not sure if that's a good approach.~~

author: think-carlo
body:
I tried to use the `Puck` component within a legacy Javascript application I work with, and found that when mounting the component the `Canvas` was broken on the initial render. For some reason the initial side-effects that should appropriately configure `zoomConfig` weren't throwing and so `zoomConfig.rootHeight`, i.e. the height of canvas, was set to `0`.

Likewise, while the width should have been set to `1280px` per my viewport (and was showing as such in the styles within Inspector Tools), it _still_ seemed like the canvas was breaking out of the parent container.

These two changes fixed the issue on my end, and should prevent them from happening for others! 
- By setting the `maxWidth` to `100%` we avoid breaking out of the parent regardless of what we programmatically need to set the width to by viewport.
- By checking to see if `zoomConfig.rootHeight` is falsey, we can set it to `"auto"`, in which case it will simply fill its available space on initial render and then re-zoomed on window resize events.

author: kazimuth
body:
# Description of Changes

Fixes issue identified in https://github.com/clockworklabs/com.clockworklabs.spacetimedbsdk/pull/264 by implementing `IEquatable<Self>` for all `[SpacetimeDB.Type]`s in C#. Also overrides `GetHashCode()` and `ToString()` for these types, which should be helpful if users want to use them as hash map keys or print them.

Ready for review.

# API and ABI breaking changes

Technically API breaking, since it is possible users manually implemented `IEquatable` somewhere.
It's an easy fix though.

This also uses `#nullable enable` and `#nullable restore` in the generated code. This requires a version of Unity supporting C# 8. But I believe we already required this.

# Expected complexity level and risk

2: this is a slightly-tricky algorithm to implement due to some pitfalls in C#'s type system.

# Testing

- [x] Get all C# module stuff compiling
- [x] Add equality proptests for a wide variety of types
- [x] Test that that SDK bug is fixed
- [ ] Test quickstart-chat
- [ ] Test blackholio
